ledger.x: c. 600 BCE: Cedi, one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas, is ruled from Suktimati in eastern Bundelkhand. 'By the 6th to 5th centuries BCE' Cedi was 'one of the more important states in Iron Age India' and the Anguttara Nikaya listed it among the 'solasa Mahajanapadas'; infobox 'Established c. 1200 BCE', 'Capital Suktimati…

c. 450 BCE: Cedi disappears from the record. The page gives 'Disestablished c. 300 BCE' and nothing on how the state ended; the Mahajanapadas page is silent too. Cliopatria ends the row in -451, the year it also ends Vatsa; no page names a conqueror, so no successor is recorded and the land is drawn…

certainty.note: The page gives neighbours (Matsya beyond the Chambal to the west, Kasi to the north-east, the Karusas in the Son valley to the east, the Dasarnas on the Dhasan) but no line; the shape is two radii around the candidate capitals.
